intro.title: Publish this registry to a common repository
intro.body: A common repository is the central node a Jadmin pings when it goes looking for data holder groups. What you name below is this deployment as a whole — your data holder group registry. Because a deployment is multi-tenant, the announcement carries its data holder groups as a list, each with the templates that group permits over there: groups set to Globally published, and within them templates set to Globally published. Nothing else leaves this host, and the repository’s own administrators review the listing before it is published.

settings.title: Publication
settings.enabled: Announce this registry to a common repository
settings.enabledHint: While this is off, nothing is sent and this deployment stays invisible to anyone who has not registered it by hand.
settings.urlHint: The repository application’s base URL — the part before /registry, not the feed itself. The backend calls this, not your browser, so it must resolve from the server: use a hostname the backend can see and the API’s port, not the admin UI’s. In the default compose stack that is http://dataholder-registry-backend:8084/dataholder-registry.
settings.identityHeading: How this registry is identified over there
settings.codeHint: Claimed on the first announcement and fixed afterwards. Requestor managers key on it.
settings.name: Registry name
settings.nameHint: The name of this deployment, not of any one data holder group — those go out as a list beneath it.
settings.baseUrlHint: Where a requestor manager should send its requests — this deployment, as the outside world reaches it.
settings.enableFirst: Turn publication on and save before announcing.
